ideas.risks: This may mainly clarify definitions rather than produce a new theorem; horizon-oblivious process-aware learnability may still collapse under a different oracle argument.
ideas.summary: Formalize the solver's quantifier-collapse observation: if the learner may depend on both the process law and the horizon, every process is learnable by repeatedly playing a horizon-optimal fixed quote up to an epsilon. Then separate the nontrivial regimes: horizon-oblivious process-aware learners, universal learners over a class, minimax learners, and post-history uniform guarantees.
ideas.title: Pin Down The Nontrivial Quantifiers
ideas.why_promising: It may completely settle which readings of the original iff are impossible before explorers spend effort proving necessity statements that are vacuous or false.

ideas.risks: The lower bound may only prove a universal-class or minimax impossibility, not an instance-wise characterization; strict crossing and unattained suprema need careful epsilon handling.
ideas.summary: Turn the two-continuation block example into a theorem. Use N initial zeros followed by a terminal price in {1/2, 1}; before the terminal observation the learner cannot know whether quotes below 1/2 or near 1 are needed. Prove that for any randomized learner one continuation has Omega(N) regret, then concatenate superexponentially growing blocks to get a class-level no-sublinear-regret result.
ideas.title: Two-Continuation Indistinguishability Lower Bound
ideas.why_promising: This is the most concrete route from raw tail failure to a real hardness theorem, and it directly targets the information-theoretic obstruction identified in the notes.

ideas.risks: A too-exact functional could become tautological or unobservable; proving both sufficiency and necessity may require strong class assumptions.
ideas.summary: Define a decision-relevant delayed-tail quantity that counts unresolved payoff only when it can change the identity or value of the best fixed quote conditional on the current history. Possible forms include a conditional value-of-information gap, a Le Cam two-continuation modulus, or a supremum over pairs of continuations that are observationally identical for h steps but have separated optimal quotes.
ideas.title: Decision-Relevant Tail Mass
ideas.why_promising: All accepted counterexamples show that raw beta, gamma, and Delta fail because delayed mass is tiny, predictable, or irrelevant. A value-of-information tail is aligned with the actual obstruction.

ideas.risks: The construction must keep expected comparator value small while maintaining positive-payoff essential-sup tails; if the rare branch is fully coded, learnability becomes trivial and the example may overlap CE-003.
ideas.summary: Build a rare-branch process with positive-probability histories containing arbitrarily long profitable delays, so beta or gamma fails by essential supremum, while the ex-ante contribution to regret is summable or o(T). A candidate is to draw a rare branch m with probability p_m, reveal or partially reveal a code, wait L_m steps, and then emit a constant-scale random terminal price with p_m L_m summable.
ideas.title: Rare-History Essential-Sup Stress Test
ideas.why_promising: It would show that uniform post-history tail conditions are too strong even at positive payoff scale, and would motivate expectation, quantile, or predictable-tail alternatives.

ideas.risks: These quantities are horizon-dependent and may still be far from necessary for learnability; they may mostly improve sufficiency rather than characterize possibility.
ideas.summary: Develop the hierarchy between Delta_T(H), the smaller comparator gap Gamma_T(H)=sup_a V_T(a)-sup_a V_T^H(a), and possible argmax-stability gaps. Prove the clean regret comparison R_T <= R_T^H + Gamma_T(H), compute Gamma on CE-001/CE-003/CE-005, and identify when Gamma_T(H_T)=o(T) is enough for truncation-based algorithms.
ideas.title: Sharper Truncation Gap Hierarchy
ideas.why_promising: It gives an immediate sharper sufficient condition and may reveal exactly which part of delayed payoff mass matters to fixed-comparator regret.

ideas.risks: Most cited algorithms are bandit or OCO results, while the market-making reduction is full-information with arm-dependent and infinite non-fill delays; the mapping may require a new wrapper rather than direct citation.
ideas.summary: Translate adaptive-delay and skipping algorithms to the finite grid market-making model. Treat unresolved fills after a chosen cutoff as skipped observations and aim for regret bounded by learning terms plus skipped payoff mass, without knowing beta, gamma, or a good H in advance. Compare residue-class Hedge, Joulani-Gyorgy-Szepesvari reductions, Gyorgy-Joulani skipping, and optimism-with-delay methods.
ideas.title: Adaptive Skipping For Grid Market Making
ideas.why_promising: It could turn the sufficient theorem into a more usable algorithm and connect predictable long delays to optimism rather than worst-case truncation loss.

ideas.risks: Adversarial time variation and delayed observation may destroy the strong one-sided-Lipschitz guarantees; naive T/K discretization may be minimax-tight for the delayed adversarial problem.
ideas.summary: Exploit that each truncated reward is a threshold function r_t^H(a)=a 1{a < M_t^H}. Study whether cumulative payoff curves have one-sided Lipschitz or posted-price structure that permits adaptive grids, binary-search-style localization, or smaller discretization regret than T/K. Cross-check against Kleinberg-Leighton and Duetting-Guruganesh-Schneider-Wang style lower bounds.
ideas.title: Threshold Geometry Beyond Uniform Grids
ideas.why_promising: The current proof treats quotes as unrelated arms after discretization, losing structure that may be crucial for sharp rates or for a cleaner characterization.

ideas.risks: This is mostly negative progress unless paired with a positive characterization; all-horizon bounds can be delicate near block boundaries.
ideas.summary: Polish the main counterexamples into standalone propositions: sparse vanishing spikes refuting beta-necessity, coded delays refuting gamma-necessity, and predictable spikes refuting Delta-necessity. For CE-005, finish the all-horizons proof for the superexponential uniform-spike variant and decide whether the binary power-of-two variant requires horizon-aware actions.
ideas.title: Counterexample Package With Exact Quantifiers
ideas.why_promising: A rigorous negative package will prevent future agents from re-proving false necessity claims and will clarify exactly which assumptions any revised theorem must include.
